content:
The image shows corn kernels covered with white/whitish fungal mycelium growing between and around the kernels, with a fluffy, cobweb-like texture. The kernels themselves appear pinkish-tan/orange in color. There is no pink/red coloration to the mold itself, and no green coloration.

Key observations:
- White fluffy mycelium between kernels
- Kernels are pinkish-tan/orange colored
- No pink/red mold (rules out Gibberella)
- No green mold (rules out Trichoderma, Aspergillus, Penicillium)
- No black pycnidia visible (rules out Diplodia)
- The mold is white/whitish, consistent with Fusarium ear rot

Fusarium ear rot description: "Whitish to pink-colored fungal growth on kernels, often at the ear tip, sometimes with a starburst pattern." The white mycelium and pinkish kernel discoloration fits well.

This could also be Diplodia, but Diplodia typically starts from the base and has visible black pycnidia. The image doesn't show base-of-ear origin clearly, and there are no obvious black structures.

The white cottony mycelium with pinkish kernel discoloration is most consistent with **Fusarium_Disease**.
